# Customize Veyon Project — CIMED ### Veyon 4.10.4 customizado para HCFMB / CiMED · Qt/C++ **Repositórios espelhados (GitLab + GitHub)** — acompanhamento contínuo e release pública; README e docs **idênticos** nos dois.

 

---

--- ## 📌 Sobre Pacote **Veyon 4.10.4 (GPLv2)** customizado para o ambiente **CiMED / HCFMB**, com: - identidade visual institucional (diálogos CIMED); - bandeja HiDPI (125% / 150% DPI); - logs de acesso com **integridade SHA-256** gravados **somente na rede** UNC; - detecção de adulteração com alerta deduplicado; - pacote portátil **`Veyon_Custom`** e instaladores win64 (lab + posto); - estabilidade da bandeja e tecla **F9** durante sessão VNC. | | | |---|---| | **Instituição** | HCFMB — CiMED | | **Produto** | Veyon CIMED — UI **versão 1.1** (sentinela/token handshake permanece **VERSÃO 1.0**) | | **Base** | Veyon 4.10.4 | | **GitLab** | | | **GitHub** | | --- ## 📸 Ilustrações / fotos ### Banner e fluxo de trabalho (GitLab)

```mermaid flowchart LR A[Código local] --> B[Commit] B --> C[Push GitLab] C --> D[Review / histórico] D --> E{Projeto pronto?} E -->|Não| A E -->|Sim| F[Push completo GitHub] ``` ### Arquitetura

### Mapa das integrações

### Bandeja HiDPI

--- ## 🏗️ Arquitetura ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph REPO["Repositório"] SRC["veyon-4.10.4-src/
código CIMED"] DEPLOY["Veyon_Custom/
binários"] DOCS["docs/"] end SRC --> BUILD["build/ local"] BUILD --> DEPLOY DEPLOY --> EXE["veyon-server / worker / master"] DEPLOY --> CORE["veyon-core.dll"] DEPLOY --> PLG["plugins/*.dll"] EXE --> UNC["\\\\172.20.100.36\\vnc_veyon$\\veyon\\"] ``` | Componente | Função CiMED | |------------|--------------| | `veyon-core.dll` | UI CIMED, bandeja HiDPI, logs, diálogos | | `veyon-server.exe` | VNC + `TamperLogProtector` | | `veyon-worker.exe` | Bandeja + vigilância de logs (poll 2 s) | | `veyon-master.exe` | Console do Administrador | | `remoteaccess.dll` | Acesso remoto com diálogo CIMED | --- ## ✨ Features CIMED | # | Entrega | Status | |---|---------|--------| | 1 | **UI CIMED** — logon, hostname, confirmar desktop, F9 | Validada | | 2 | **Bandeja HiDPI** — supersampling / multi-DPR | Validada | | 3 | **Deploy `Veyon_Custom`** | Validada | | 4 | **Logs na rede** UNC `vnc_veyon$` | Validada | | 5 | **Integridade SHA-256** + alerta único | Validada | | 6 | **Worker estável** com VNC ativo | Validada | | 7 | **Instaladores win64** lab + posto | Validada | | 8 | **Shared-connection** — pilha de hovers UDP (piloto frota) | Validada (lab `.86`/`.119`) | | 9 | **DistributeFiles permanente** + guard GPO | Validada | | 10 | **RA close → Ocioso** sem fechar Master | Validada | **Planejado (fora do escopo atual):** proteção por senha em log de processo, fallback hostname VM/NAT, watchdog avançado. --- ## 🖥️ Telas CIMED ```mermaid flowchart LR LOGON["Logon"] --> PD["PasswordDialog"] HOST["Hostname/IP"] --> CHD["CimedHostInputDialog"] VNC["Confirmar desktop"] --> DAC["DesktopAccessConfirmDialog"] F9["Tecla F9"] --> CSI["ComputerSupportInfoDialog"] PD --> STYLE["CimedDialogStyle"] CHD --> STYLE DAC --> STYLE ```

| Tela | Arquivo | Quando | |------|---------|--------| | Logon | `PasswordDialog.cpp` | Autenticação no Master | | Hostname/IP | `CimedHostInputDialog.cpp` | Acesso remoto manual | | Confirmar desktop | `DesktopAccessConfirmDialog.cpp` | Usuário autoriza VNC | | F9 | `ComputerSupportInfoDialog.cpp` | Suporte (IP, hostname, versão) | --- ## 📂 Estrutura do repositório ```text Projeto Veyon/ ├── veyon-4.10.4-src (1)/veyon-4.10.4/ # código-fonte CIMED │ ├── core/src/ # logs, bandeja, UI │ ├── server/src/ # VNC + tamper │ ├── master/src/ # console / F11 │ ├── worker/ # bandeja + vigia │ └── plugins/remoteaccess/ ├── Veyon_Custom/ # pacote de deploy (binários) ├── docs/ # relatórios + imagens ├── installer/ · scripts/ · tools/ └── README.md # este arquivo ``` | Pasta | Conteúdo | |-------|----------| | `veyon-4.10.4-src (1)/veyon-4.10.4/` | Código alterado | | `Veyon_Custom/` | Pacote portátil | | `docs/` | Relatórios, fotos, fluxogramas | | `installer/` · `scripts/` | Pipeline de instaladores | --- ## 📚 Documentação Botões com links **relativos** (funcionam no GitLab, GitHub e clone local):

--- ## 🚀 Build / deploy ```bash # Acompanhar / clonar a partir do GitLab git clone https://gitlab.com/developercanon/customizedveyonproject.git cd customizedveyonproject ``` Build (resumo — detalhes em `VEYON_CIMED_CUSTOM_LEIA-ME.txt` e `scripts/`): 1. Configure toolchain MinGW/CMake no fonte `veyon-4.10.4-src (1)/veyon-4.10.4/` 2. Compile e copie artefatos para `Veyon_Custom/` 3. Gere instaladores via `scripts/build_veyon_custom_installer.ps1` (win64-dual) ```powershell powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build_veyon_custom_installer.ps1 -Architecture win64-dual /* … truncado na árvore (arquivo completo no GitHub) … */

nodes.title: build_veyon_custom_win32.ps1
nodes.code:
# Compila Veyon CIMED 32-bit completo (i686) e gera Veyon_Custom_win32
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$Root = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path)
$DockerScript = Join-Path $Root "scripts\build_veyon_custom_win32_docker.ps1"

if (-not (Test-Path $DockerScript)) {
    throw "Script Docker nao encontrado: $DockerScript"
}

& $DockerScript
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
    throw @"
Falha ao compilar Veyon CIMED 32-bit completo.

O pacote 32-bit com TODAS as customizacoes CIMED exige a imagem Docker do Veyon CI
(registry.gitlab.com/veyon/ci-mingw-w64:main), pois o MSYS2 local nao oferece Qt6 para i686.

1) Instale e inicie o Docker Desktop:
     winget install Docker.DockerDesktop
2) Execute novamente:
     powershell -File scripts\build_veyon_custom_win32.ps1
3) Depois gere o instalador:
     powershell -File scripts\build_veyon_custom_installer.ps1 -Architecture win32
"@
}

nodes.title: build_veyon_custom_win32_docker.ps1
nodes.code:
# Compila Veyon CIMED 32-bit completo (i686) via Docker (Fedora + mingw32 Qt6)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$Root = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path)
$Src = Join-Path $Root "veyon-4.10.4-src (1)\veyon-4.10.4"
$OutCustom = Join-Path $Root "Veyon_Custom_win32"
$Dockerfile = Join-Path $Root "docker\Dockerfile.veyon-mingw-i686"
$LocalImage = "veyon-cimed-mingw-i686:latest"

if (-not (Test-Path $Src)) {
    throw "Fonte nao encontrada: $Src"
}
if (-not (Test-Path $Dockerfile)) {
    throw "Dockerfile nao encontrado: $Dockerfile"
}

$dockerExe = @(
    "${env:ProgramFiles}\Docker\Docker\resources\bin\docker.exe",
    "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Docker\Docker\resources\bin\docker.exe"
) | Where-Object { Test-Path $_ } | Select-Object -First 1

if (-not $dockerExe) {
    $dockerCmd = Get-Command docker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($dockerCmd) { $dockerExe = $dockerCmd.Source }
}

if (-not $dockerExe) {
    throw "Docker nao encontrado. Instale Docker Desktop e aguarde status 'running'."
}

Write-Host "Usando Docker: $dockerExe"
& $dockerExe ps 2>&1 | Out-Null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Docker Desktop nao esta respondendo. Abra o Docker e aguarde ficar 'running'." }

Write-Host "Construindo imagem local $LocalImage (primeira vez demora)..."
& $dockerExe build -t $LocalImage -f $Dockerfile $Root
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "docker build falhou para $LocalImage" }

Write-Host "Compilando veyon-win32 com codigo CIMED (i686)..."
$outDir = Join-Path $Root "dist\docker-win32-out"

cd /veyon

/usr/i686-w64-mingw32/bin/qt6/qt-cmake /veyon -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DQT_TRANSLATIONS_DIR=/usr/share/qt6/translations

# Prepara Veyon_Custom_win32 a partir do instalador oficial Veyon 4.10.4 (win32)
# Necessario porque MSYS2 nao oferece Qt6 i686 para compilar o codigo CIMED localmente.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$Root = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path)
$OutCustom = Join-Path $Root "Veyon_Custom_win32"
$Cache = Join-Path $Root "dist\cache"
$SetupUrl = "https://github.com/veyon/veyon/releases/download/v4.10.4/veyon-4.10.4.0-win32-setup.exe"
$SetupFile = Join-Path $Cache "veyon-4.10.4.0-win32-setup.exe"
$ExtractDir = Join-Path $Cache "veyon-win32-extract"

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $Cache -Force | Out-Null

if (-not (Test-Path $SetupFile)) {
    Write-Host "Baixando Veyon oficial win32..."
    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $SetupUrl -OutFile $SetupFile -UseBasicParsing
}

$7z = @(
    "${env:ProgramFiles}\7-Zip\7z.exe",
    "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\7-Zip\7z.exe"
) | Where-Object { Test-Path $_ } | Select-Object -First 1

if (-not $7z) {
    throw "7-Zip nao encontrado. Instale: winget install 7zip.7zip"
}

if (Test-Path $ExtractDir) { Remove-Item $ExtractDir -Recurse -Force }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $ExtractDir -Force | Out-Null

Write-Host "Extraindo instalador oficial..."
& $7z x $SetupFile "-o$ExtractDir" -y | Out-Null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "7z falhou ao extrair win32 setup" }

# NSIS solid LZMA: arquivos ficam em $PLUGINSDIR ou raiz da extracao
$payloadRoot = @(
    (Join-Path $ExtractDir '$PLUGINSDIR'),
    (Join-Path $ExtractDir 'PLUGINSDIR'),
    $ExtractDir
) | Where-Object { Test-Path (Join-Path $_ 'veyon-core.dll') } | Select-Object -First 1

if (-not $payloadRoot) {
    $payloadRoot = Get-ChildItem $ExtractDir -Recurse -Filter 'veyon-core.dll' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Select-Object -First 1 |
        ForEach-Object { $_.Directory.FullName }
}

if (-not $payloadRoot -or -not (Test-Path (Join-Path $payloadRoot 'veyon-core.dll'))) {
    throw "Nao foi possivel localizar veyon-core.dll na extracao do instalador win32"
}

Write-Host "Payload win32 encontrado em: $payloadRoot"

if (Test-Path $OutCustom) { Remove-Item $OutCustom -Recurse -Force }
Copy-Item $payloadRoot $OutCustom -Recurse -Force

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Join-Path $OutCustom "logs\acessos_veyon") -Force | Out-Null
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Join-Path $OutCustom "logs\acessos_veyon_ad") -Force | Out-Null

if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $OutCustom "COPYING")) -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $OutCustom "LICENSE.TXT"))) {
    Copy-Item (Join-Path $OutCustom "LICENSE.TXT") (Join-Path $OutCustom "COPYING")
}

$readme = @"
Veyon CIMED - pacote 32-bit (base oficial Veyon 4.10.4)

Este pacote foi montado a partir do instalador oficial win32 porque o ambiente
local nao possui Qt6 32-bit para compilar as customizacoes CIMED.

Instalador: fluxo CIMED (servico, pastas de log, atalhos).
Binarios: Veyon 4.10.4 oficial (sem patches CIMED de codigo-fonte).

Para 64-bit com todas as customizacoes CIMED, use Veyon-CIMED-1.0-win64-setup.exe.
"@
Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $OutCustom "README-CIMED-WIN32.txt") -Value $readme -Encoding UTF8

if (Test-Path "C:\msys64\mingw64\bin\objdump.exe") {
    & "C:\msys64\mingw64\bin\objdump.exe" -f (Join-Path $OutCustom "veyon-core.dll") | Select-String "file format"
}

Write-Host "Veyon_Custom_win32 pronto (base oficial)."

# Relatório Técnico — Veyon CIMED 1.0 | | | |---|---| | **Instituição** | HCFMB — CiMED | | **Produto** | Veyon CIMED — UI **1.1** (sentinela/token **VERSÃO 1.0**) | | **Repositório** | [CustomizeVeyonProject](https://github.com/CanonEngineer/CustomizeVeyonProject) | | **Data** | 26/06/2026 | | **Público** | Diretoria, conferência técnica, gestão de TI | | **Documento complementar** | `RELATORIO-ESTRUTURA-CODIGO-CIMED.md` (detalhamento de código) | --- ## 1. Resumo executivo O projeto customiza o Veyon 4.10.4 para o ambiente CiMED, entregando **identidade visual institucional**, **pacote portátil de deploy** (`Veyon_Custom`), **logs de acesso com integridade SHA-256 gravados somente na rede** e **estabilidade do processo de bandeja** durante sessões VNC ativas. Todas as entregas listadas neste relatório foram **implantadas e validadas** em ambiente real, preservando login, CONECTAR, fluxo VNC, registro de acessos e tecla **F9** (informações do computador). **Resultado principal:** solução pronta para operação em laboratórios e postos gerenciados, com rastreabilidade de acessos na rede institucional e interface alinhada à marca CiMED. --- ## 2. Problema e objetivo | Aspecto | Situação anterior | Objetivo CiMED | |---------|-------------------|----------------| | Interface | Diálogos genéricos Qt | Telas institucionais padronizadas | | Bandeja | Ícones pixelados em 125%/150% DPI | Ícones nítidos em monitores HiDPI | | Logs | Risco de cópia local desalinhada | Escrita **única** no share UNC | | Operação | Worker lento com VNC ativo | Bandeja e F9 responsivos em sessão | --- ## 3. Entregas validadas | # | Entrega | Benefício para a instituição | |---|---------|------------------------------| | 1 | **UI CIMED** — 4 diálogos (logon, hostname, confirmar desktop, F9) | Experiência única e profissional ao Administrador e ao Usuário | | 2 | **Bandeja HiDPI** | Status de conexão legível em qualquer escala Windows | | 3 | **Deploy `Veyon_Custom`** | Instalação portátil organizada como o instalador oficial | | 4 | **Logs na rede** | Auditoria centralizada em `\\172.20.100.36\vnc_veyon$\veyon\` | | 5 | **Integridade SHA-256** | Detecção de adulteração com alerta deduplicado | | 6 | **Worker estável** | Hover e F9 funcionam durante monitoramento VNC | **Fora do escopo atual (planejado):** proteção por senha em log de processo, fallback hostname VM/NAT, watchdog avançado. --- ## 4. Arquitetura resumida ![Mapa das integrações Veyon CIMED](imagens/mapa-integracoes.png)

Figura 1 — Visão das integrações implantadas (UI, deploy, logs e bandeja).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Captura telas CIMED reais via Qt (PySide6) com os mesmos PNGs e estilos do projeto."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from PySide6.QtCore import Qt, QTimer
from PySide6.QtGui import QColor, QFont, QGuiApplication, QIcon, QImage, QPainter, QPainterPath, QPixmap
from PySide6.QtWidgets import (
    QApplication,
    QDialog,
    QFrame,
    QGridLayout,
    QHBoxLayout,
    QLabel,
    QLineEdit,
    QPushButton,
    QVBoxLayout,
    QWidget,
)

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RES = ROOT / "veyon-4.10.4-src (1)" / "veyon-4.10.4" / "core" / "resources"
OUT = ROOT / "docs" / "imagens" / "telas-cimed"

DIALOG_W, DIALOG_H = 560, 420
TALL_H = 500
BRAND_W = 186


def load_logo(max_width: int = 148) -> QPixmap:
    path = RES / "cimed-logo.png"
    image = QImage(str(path))
    image = image.convertToFormat(QImage.Format.Format_ARGB32)
    w, h = image.width(), image.height()
    min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y = w, h, 0, 0
    for y in range(h):
        for x in range(w):
            if image.pixelColor(x, y).alpha() > 8:
                min_x, min_y = min(min_x, x), min(min_y, y)
                max_x, max_y = max(max_x, x), max(max_y, y)
    cropped = image.copy(min_x, min_y, max_x - min_x + 1, max_y - min_y + 1)
    return QPixmap.fromImage(cropped).scaledToWidth(max_width, Qt.TransformationMode.SmoothTransformation)


def dialog_stylesheet() -> str:
    return (
        "QDialog {"
        "  background-color: qlineargradient(x1:0,y1:0,x2:1,y2:1,"
        "    stop:0 #07101f, stop:0.45 #0c2344, stop:1 #050b14);"
        "}"
    )


def header_widget(parent: QWidget, title: str) -> QWidget:
    w = QWidget(parent)
    w.setStyleSheet(
        "background-color: rgba(8, 20, 40, 0.94);"
        "border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(34, 211, 238, 0.55);"
    )
    lay = QHBoxLayout(w)
    lay.setContentsMargins(16, 10, 16, 10)
    lbl = QLabel(title, w)
    lbl.setStyleSheet("font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; color: #e2e8f0;")
    lay.addWidget(lbl)
    lay.addStretch()
    return w


def brand_panel(parent: QWidget) -> QWidget:
    panel = QWidget(parent)
    panel.setFixedWidth(BRAND_W)
    lay = QVBoxLayout(panel)
    lay.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
    lay.addStretch(1)

    card = QFrame(panel)
    card.setObjectName("cimedBrandCard")
    card.setStyleSheet(
        "#cimedBrandCard {"
        "  background-color: qlineargradient(x1:0,y1:0,x2:0,y2:1,"
        "    stop:0 #0a1a33, stop:0.38 #2563eb, stop:0.55 #38bdf8, stop:1 #07101f);"
        "  border: 1px solid rgba(125, 211, 252, 0.85);"
        "  border-radius: 14px;"
        "}"
    )
    card_lay = QVBoxLayout(card)
    card_lay.setContentsMargins(10, 14, 10, 14)
    logo = QLabel(card)
    logo.setAlignment(Qt.AlignmentFlag.AlignHCenter)
    logo.setPixmap(load_logo())
    card_lay.addWidget(logo)
    title = QLabel("CiMED", card)
    title.setAlignment(Qt.AlignmentFlag.AlignHCenter)
    title.setStyleSheet("font-size: 15px; font-weight: 800; color: #f8fafc; letter-spacing: 1px;")

param(

    [switch]$StatusOnly

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$InstallDir = "C:\Program Files\Veyon"
$RegBase = "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Veyon Solutions\Veyon"
$RestoreScript = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\Veyon_Custom\_deploy\restore-funcional-20260707\RESTAURAR-FUNCIONAL-20260707.ps1"
$PatchedCore = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\dist\msys64-win64-core\veyon-core.dll"
$PatchedServer = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\dist\msys64-win64-core\veyon-server.exe"
$PatchedWorker = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\dist\msys64-win64-core\veyon-worker.exe"
$LogFile = Join-Path $InstallDir "logs\VeyonServer.log"

function Show-Status {
    Write-Host "`n=== MULTI-MONITOR .86 ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    reg query "$RegBase\UltraVNC" /v MultiMonitorSupport 2>$null
    reg query "$RegBase\Service" /v MultiMonitorSupport 2>$null
    $core = Get-Item (Join-Path $InstallDir "veyon-core.dll")
    Write-Host "veyon-core.dll: $($core.Length) bytes, hash $((Get-FileHash $core -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.Substring(0,16))..."
    Get-Service VeyonService | Format-Table Name, Status
    if (Test-Path $LogFile) {
        Select-String -Path $LogFile -Pattern "QueryScreens|bitmap dimensions|APPCRASH|Monitorando" |
            Select-Object -Last 6 |
            ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $($_.Line.Substring(0, [Math]::Min(180, $_.Line.Length)))" }
    }
}

if ($StatusOnly) { Show-Status; exit 0 }

if (-not $SkipRestore -and (Test-Path $RestoreScript)) {
    Write-Host "Restaurando binarios funcionais..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    & $RestoreScript -InstallDir $InstallDir
}

Write-Host "Configurando multi-monitor (captura todas as telas)..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
# MultiMonitor=true captura VirtualScreen (ex.: 3200x901). DeskDup=false evita crash DDEngine.
reg add "$RegBase\UltraVNC" /v MultiMonitorSupport /t REG_SZ /d true /f | Out-Null
reg add "$RegBase\Service" /v MultiMonitorSupport /t REG_SZ /d true /f | Out-Null
reg add "$RegBase\UltraVNC" /v DeskDupEngine /t REG_SZ /d false /f | Out-Null
reg add "$RegBase\Service" /v ConfirmAccess /t REG_SZ /d false /f | Out-Null
reg add "$RegBase\Logging" /v LogLevel /t REG_DWORD /d 5 /f | Out-Null

if (Test-Path $PatchedCore) {

    Stop-Service VeyonService -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Get-Process veyon-server, veyon-worker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
    Copy-Item -Force $PatchedCore (Join-Path $InstallDir "veyon-core.dll")
    if (Test-Path $PatchedServer) { Copy-Item -Force $PatchedServer (Join-Path $InstallDir "veyon-server.exe") }
    if (Test-Path $PatchedWorker) { Copy-Item -Force $PatchedWorker (Join-Path $InstallDir "veyon-worker.exe") }
} else {
    Write-Host "Patch core nao encontrado em dist/docker-win64-core (compile depois)." -ForegroundColor DarkYellow
    Stop-Service VeyonService -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Get-Process veyon-server, veyon-worker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
}

Start-Service VeyonService
Start-Sleep -Seconds 6
Write-Host "Pronto. Conecte da .119 e verifique menu: All screens / Screen 1 / Screen 2" -ForegroundColor Green
Show-Status

        Copy-Item -Force $from $to
        Write-Host "  OK $(Split-Path $to -Leaf) ($((Get-Item $to).Length) bytes)" -ForegroundColor Green
    }

# Corrige conflito Veyon (.86) x TightVNC e reinicia limpo para conexao .119 -> .86
param(
    [switch]$Apply,
    [switch]$DisableTightVnc,
    [switch]$StatusOnly
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
$RemoteIp = "186.217.65.119"
$LogFile = "C:\Program Files\Veyon\logs\VeyonServer.log"
$RegBase = "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Veyon Solutions\Veyon"

function Write-Section([string]$Title) {
    Write-Host "`n=== $Title ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
}

function Get-ConnectionHealth {
    $tcp119 = @(Get-NetTCPConnection -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { $_.RemoteAddress -eq $RemoteIp -and $_.LocalPort -eq 11100 -and $_.State -eq "Established" })
    $vncLocal = @(Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 11200 -State Established -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
    $tvn = Get-Process tvnserver -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    $veyon = Get-Process veyon-server,veyon-worker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    $framebufferOk = $false
    if (Test-Path $LogFile) {
        $tail = Get-Content $LogFile -Tail 200 -Encoding UTF8 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        $framebufferOk = @($tail | Where-Object {
            $_ -match "request client buffer\[[1-9][0-9]{6,}\]" -or
            $_ -match "rawdata=[1-9]" -or
            $_ -match "transmitted=[1-9]"
        }).Count -gt 0
    }

    return [ordered]@{
        tcpFrom119 = $tcp119.Count -gt 0
        vncLocal11200 = $vncLocal.Count -gt 0
        tightVncRunning = [bool]$tvn
        veyonProcesses = @($veyon | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Name):$($_.Id)" })
        framebufferSending = $framebufferOk
    }
}

function Show-Status {
    Write-Section "STATUS CONEXAO .119 -> .86"
    $h = Get-ConnectionHealth
    Write-Host "TCP .119 -> :11100 ESTABLISHED : $(if ($h.tcpFrom119) { 'SIM' } else { 'NAO' })" -ForegroundColor $(if ($h.tcpFrom119) { "Green" } else { "Yellow" })
    Write-Host "VNC local :11200 ESTABLISHED   : $(if ($h.vncLocal11200) { 'SIM' } else { 'NAO' })" -ForegroundColor $(if ($h.vncLocal11200) { "Green" } else { "Red" })
    Write-Host "TightVNC (tvnserver) rodando  : $(if ($h.tightVncRunning) { 'SIM - CONFLITO!' } else { 'NAO - OK' })" -ForegroundColor $(if ($h.tightVncRunning) { "Red" } else { "Green" })
    Write-Host "Framebuffer enviado (log)     : $(if ($h.framebufferSending) { 'SIM' } else { 'NAO / ainda nao' })" -ForegroundColor $(if ($h.framebufferSending) { "Green" } else { "Yellow" })
    Write-Host "Processos Veyon               : $(if ($h.veyonProcesses.Count) { ($h.veyonProcesses -join ', ') } else { 'nenhum' })"

    $svc = Get-Service tvnserver -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($svc) {
        Write-Host "Servico TightVNC              : $($svc.Status) / $($svc.StartType)"
    }

    if (Test-Path $LogFile) {
        Write-Host "`n--- Ultimos eventos criticos ---"
        Select-String -Path $LogFile -Pattern "Recurso solicitado|WinVNCAPPMain|rawdata=|ProxyConnectionClosed|Monitorando|CheckBuffer.*client buffer" |
            Select-Object -Last 8 |
            ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $($_.Line.Substring(0, [Math]::Min(160, $_.Line.Length)))" }
    }
}

function Apply-Fix {
    Write-Section "APLICANDO CORRECAO"

    # 1) TightVNC compete pelo driver de video ("Recurso solicitado em uso") e impede framebuffer
    Write-Host "Parando TightVNC..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Stop-Service tvnserver -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Get-Process tvnserver -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2

    if ($DisableTightVnc) {
        Write-Host "Desabilitando servico TightVNC (nao reinicia no boot)..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
        Set-Service tvnserver -StartupType Disabled -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }

    # 2) UltraVNC: evitar DDEngine + dual monitor instavel nesta maquina
    Write-Host "Ajustando registry Veyon/UltraVNC..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    reg add "$RegBase\UltraVNC" /v DeskDupEngine /t REG_SZ /d false /f | Out-Null
    reg add "$RegBase\UltraVNC" /v MultiMonitorSupport /t REG_SZ /d false /f | Out-Null
    reg add "$RegBase\UltraVNC" /v PollFullScreen /t REG_SZ /d true /f | Out-Null
    reg add "$RegBase\Service" /v MultiMonitorSupport /t REG_SZ /d false /f | Out-Null
    reg add "$RegBase\Logging" /v LogLevel /t REG_DWORD /d 5 /f | Out-Null

    # 3) Reinicio limpo Veyon
    Write-Host "Reiniciando VeyonService..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Get-Process veyon-master -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force
    Stop-Service VeyonService -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Get-Process veyon-server,veyon-worker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 4
    Start-Service VeyonService
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 6

    Write-Host "`nCorrecao aplicada." -ForegroundColor Green
    Write-Host "Faca a conexao na .119 AGORA e rode:" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Write-Host "  powershell -File scripts\debug_live_connection_119_86.ps1 -Watch" -ForegroundColor White
}

if (-not ($Apply -or $DisableTightVnc -or $StatusOnly)) {
    Write-Host @"
Uso:
  -StatusOnly              : diagnostico rapido (sem alterar nada)
  -Apply                   : para TightVNC + ajusta registry + reinicia Veyon
  -Apply -DisableTightVnc  : idem + desabilita TightVNC no boot (recomendado)

Causa raiz encontrada: TightVNC (tvnserver) rodando junto com Veyon UltraVNC.
Sintoma: auth OK, tray 'Monitorando', mas spinner infinito (0 bytes de tela).
"@
    exit 0
}

Show-Status
if ($Apply -or $DisableTightVnc) {
    Apply-Fix
    Show-Status
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Simulate 10-hover stack layout (compress + 2 columns) and optionally inject via IPC."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import math
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

# Reuse IPC helpers from sibling script
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from test_hover_stack_ipc import OP_ADD, OP_REMOVE, pack_outbound, send  # noqa: E402

MIN_SCALE = 0.85
GAP_NORMAL = 4
GAP_COMPACT = 2
COL_GAP = 8
SCREEN_MARGIN = 4


@dataclass
class Rect:
    x: int
    y: int
    w: int
    h: int

    @property
    def right(self) -> int:
        return self.x + self.w

    @property
    def bottom(self) -> int:
        return self.y + self.h

    def overlaps(self, other: "Rect") -> bool:
        return not (
            self.right <= other.x
            or other.right <= self.x
            or self.bottom <= other.y
            or other.bottom <= self.y
        )


def scaled_size(base_w: int, base_h: int, scale: float) -> tuple[int, int]:
    # Mirror TrayHoverPopup: icon/margins shrink but stay readable (>= ~0.85).
    w = max(220 + 36 + 20, int(round(base_w * scale)))
    h = max(36 + 12, int(round(base_h * scale)))
    return w, h


def height_for_columns(heights: list[int], columns: int, gap: int) -> int:
    n = len(heights)
    if columns <= 1:
        total = sum(heights)
        if n > 1:
            total += (n - 1) * gap
        return total
    total = 0
    rows = 0
    for order in range(0, n, 2):
        left = n - 1 - order
        right = left - 1
        row_h = heights[left]
        if right >= 0:
            row_h = max(row_h, heights[right])
        total += row_h
        rows += 1
    if rows > 1:
        total += (rows - 1) * gap
    return total


def layout_stack(
    n: int,
    base_w: int,
    base_h: int,
    available_top: int,
    available_left: int,
    available_right: int,
    stack_bottom_base: int,
    stack_x: int,
) -> dict:
    max_stack_h = max(0, stack_bottom_base - available_top - SCREEN_MARGIN)
    scale = 1.0
    gap = GAP_NORMAL
    columns = 1

    def measure(sc: float) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        return [scaled_size(base_w, base_h, sc) for _ in range(n)]

    sizes = measure(1.0)
    heights = [h for _, h in sizes]
    natural = height_for_columns(heights, 1, GAP_NORMAL)

    if max_stack_h > 0 and natural > max_stack_h:
        scale = max(MIN_SCALE, min(1.0, max_stack_h / natural))
        gap = GAP_COMPACT if scale < 0.97 else GAP_NORMAL
        sizes = measure(scale)
        heights = [h for _, h in sizes]
        if height_for_columns(heights, 1, gap) > max_stack_h:
            columns = 2
            sizes = measure(1.0)
            heights = [h for _, h in sizes]
            gap = GAP_COMPACT
            two_nat = height_for_columns(heights, 2, gap)
            if two_nat > max_stack_h:
                scale = max(MIN_SCALE, min(1.0, max_stack_h / two_nat))
                sizes = measure(scale)
                heights = [h for _, h in sizes]
            else:
                scale = 1.0

    rects: list[Rect] = [Rect(0, 0, 0, 0) for _ in range(n)]
    stack_bottom = stack_bottom_base

    if columns == 1:
        for order in range(n):
            i = n - 1 - order
            w, h = sizes[i]
            x = stack_x - w // 2
            y = stack_bottom - h
            x = max(available_left + SCREEN_MARGIN, min(x, available_right - w - SCREEN_MARGIN))
            y = max(available_top + SCREEN_MARGIN, y)
            rects[i] = Rect(x, y, w, h)
            stack_bottom = y - gap
    else:
        for order in range(0, n, 2):
            left_i = n - 1 - order
            right_i = left_i - 1
            lw, lh = sizes[left_i]
            rw, rh = sizes[right_i] if right_i >= 0 else (0, 0)
            row_h = max(lh, rh) if right_i >= 0 else lh
            y = max(available_top + SCREEN_MARGIN, stack_bottom - row_h)
            left_x = stack_x - (COL_GAP // 2) - lw
            right_x = stack_x + (COL_GAP // 2)
            pair_w = (lw + COL_GAP + rw) if right_i >= 0 else lw
            pair_left = left_x if right_i >= 0 else (stack_x - lw // 2)
            pair_left = max(
                available_left + SCREEN_MARGIN,
                min(pair_left, available_right - pair_w - SCREEN_MARGIN),
            )
            if right_i >= 0:
                left_x = pair_left
                right_x = left_x + lw + COL_GAP
            else:
                left_x = pair_left
            rects[left_i] = Rect(left_x, y + (row_h - lh), lw, lh)
            if right_i >= 0:
                rects[right_i] = Rect(right_x, y + (row_h - rh), rw, rh)
            stack_bottom = y - gap

    overlaps = 0
    for a in range(n):
        for b in range(a + 1, n):
            if rects[a].overlaps(rects[b]):
                overlaps += 1

    offscreen = sum(
        1
        for r in rects
        if r.y < available_top
        or r.bottom > stack_bottom_base + 20
        or r.x < available_left
        or r.right > available_right
    )

    # Standardization: widths equal; same scale; column x alignment when 2-col
    widths = {r.w for r in rects}
    left_xs = sorted({rects[n - 1 - o].x for o in range(0, n, 2)})
    right_xs = sorted(
        {rects[n - 2 - o].x for o in range(0, n, 2) if n - 2 - o >= 0}
    )

    return {
        "n": n,
        "scale": round(scale, 3),
        "gap": gap,
        "columns": columns,
        "max_stack_h": max_stack_h,
        "used_h": stack_bottom_base - min(r.y for r in rects),
        "overlaps": overlaps,
        "offscreen": offscreen,
        "uniform_width": len(widths) == 1,
        "left_x_aligned": len(left_xs) <= 1,
        "right_x_aligned": len(right_xs) <= 1,
        "min_font_ok": scale >= MIN_SCALE,
        "rects": rects,
    }


def ascii_map(result: dict, available_top: int, stack_bottom_base: int, avail_w: int) -> str:
    height = max(20, (stack_bottom_base - available_top) // 8)
    width = 60

        ch = str(i % 10)
        for y in range(gy0, gy1 + 1):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Inject synthetic outbound tray sessions via Windows named pipe (no pywin32)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ctypes
import struct
import sys
import time
import uuid
from ctypes import wintypes

GENERIC_WRITE = 0x40000000
OPEN_EXISTING = 3
FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL = 0x80
INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE = ctypes.c_void_p(-1).value

kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
kernel32.CreateFileW.argtypes = [
    wintypes.LPCWSTR,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    wintypes.LPVOID,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    wintypes.HANDLE,
]
kernel32.CreateFileW.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
kernel32.WriteFile.argtypes = [
    wintypes.HANDLE,
    wintypes.LPCVOID,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    ctypes.POINTER(wintypes.DWORD),
    wintypes.LPVOID,
]
kernel32.WriteFile.restype = wintypes.BOOL
kernel32.CloseHandle.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE]
kernel32.CloseHandle.restype = wintypes.BOOL

MAGIC = 0x56545934
OP_ADD = 0
OP_REMOVE = 1
STATUS_CONNECTED = 3


def qstring(value: str) -> bytes:
    # QDataStream default byte order is big-endian; QString UTF-16 follows stream order.
    data = value.encode("utf-16be")
    return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + data


def pack_outbound(op: int, session_id: str, user: str, local_host: str, local_ip: str,
                  dest_host: str, dest_ip: str) -> bytes:
    return (
        struct.pack(">I", MAGIC)
        + struct.pack(">i", op)
        + qstring(session_id)
        + struct.pack(">i", STATUS_CONNECTED)
        + qstring(user)
        + qstring(local_host)
        + qstring(local_ip)
        + qstring(dest_host)
        + qstring(dest_ip)
    )


def send(pipe_name: str, payload: bytes) -> None:
    path = rf"\\.\pipe\{pipe_name}"
    handle = kernel32.CreateFileW(path, GENERIC_WRITE, 0, None, OPEN_EXISTING, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, None)
    if handle in (None, wintypes.HANDLE(-1).value, INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE):
        err = ctypes.get_last_error()
        raise OSError(err, f"CreateFile failed for {path}")
    try:
        written = wintypes.DWORD(0)
        ok = kernel32.WriteFile(handle, payload, len(payload), ctypes.byref(written), None)
        if not ok:
            raise OSError(ctypes.get_last_error(), "WriteFile failed")
    finally:
        kernel32.CloseHandle(handle)


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--pipe", default="VeyonLocalTray-0")
    parser.add_argument("--count", type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument("--hold-seconds", type=float, default=8.0)
    parser.add_argument("--remove", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.count < 1 or args.count > 10:
        print("count must be 1..10", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    sessions = []
    for i in range(args.count):
        sid = str(uuid.uuid4())
        dest_host = f"HOST-{i + 1}"
        dest_ip = f"186.217.65.{100 + i}"
        payload = pack_outbound(
            OP_ADD,
            sid,
            "testuser",
            "CIMED-ALESSAN",
            "186.217.65.86",
            dest_host,
            dest_ip,
        )
        send(args.pipe, payload)
        sessions.append(sid)
        print(f"ADD {i + 1}/{args.count} session={sid} dest={dest_host} [{dest_ip}]")
        time.sleep(0.25)

    print(f"Injected stack size={args.count}. Holding {args.hold_seconds}s...")
    time.sleep(args.hold_seconds)

    if args.remove:
        order = list(range(args.count))
        if args.count >= 2:
            mid = args.count // 2
            order = [mid] + [i for i in order if i != mid]
        for idx in order:
            sid = sessions[idx]
            payload = pack_outbound(OP_REMOVE, sid, "", "", "", "", "")
            send(args.pipe, payload)
            print(f"REMOVE session={sid}")
            time.sleep(0.4)

    print("Done.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

## Bug Description

  - Idle: Works on taskbar, fails on hover

  - Authenticating: Only blue dot, no custom icon
  - Session Active: Works on taskbar, fails on hover (still green dot + eye)

  - Error: Never seen

## Hypotheses
1. The QIcon being set on QSystemTrayIcon doesn't have all necessary sizes for Windows hover
2. The overlay icon or QWindow icon is overriding the tray icon behavior
3. The Windows shell is caching old tray icon data
4. The status indicator mapping has an issue where some states aren't triggering the custom draw functions
5. The tooltip text with Unicode characters is interfering with the icon display

## Log Collection Plan
- Instrument SystemTrayIcon::updateIcon() to log:
  - Current status indicator
  - Icon sizes being generated
  - Whether QSystemTrayIcon::setIcon() is called

- Instrument ComputerControlServer::updateTrayIconToolTip() to log:

  - Tooltip text being sent

2. O `worker` recebe as mensagens, mas o enum `StatusIndicator` chega com valor incorreto e o desenho cai no estado cinza.
3. O tooltip rico e enviado, mas uma mensagem posterior o sobrescreve com texto simples.
4. O pacote `Veyon_Custom` esta carregando um binario antigo de `veyon-core.dll` ou `veyon-worker.exe`.

## Plano
1. Inspecionar o fluxo de envio e recebimento das mensagens do tray.
2. Adicionar instrumentacao minima em `server` e `worker`.
3. Recompilar apenas os binarios minimos.
4. Validar `server -> worker -> tray` no `Veyon_Custom`.

nodes.code:
# Veyon - Virtual Eye On Networks

[![.github/workflows/build.yml](https://github.com/veyon/veyon/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg?branch=4.5)](https://github.com/veyon/veyon/actions/workflows/build.yml)
[![Latest stable release](https://img.shields.io/github/release/veyon/veyon.svg?maxAge=3600)](https://github.com/veyon/veyon/releases)
[![Overall downloads on Github](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/veyon/veyon/total.svg?maxAge=3600)](https://github.com/veyon/veyon/releases)
[![Documentation Status](https://readthedocs.org/projects/veyon/badge/?version=latest)](https://docs.veyon.io/)
[![Localise on Transifex](https://img.shields.io/badge/localise-on_transifex-green.svg)](https://app.transifex.com/veyon-solutions/veyon/)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPLv2-green.svg)](LICENSE)


## What is Veyon?

Veyon is a free and open source software for monitoring and controlling
computers across multiple platforms. Veyon supports you in teaching in digital
learning environments, performing virtual trainings or giving remote support.

The following features are available in Veyon:

  * Overview: monitor all computers in one or multiple locations or classrooms
  * Remote access: view or control computers to watch and support users
  * Demo: broadcast the teacher's screen in realtime (fullscreen/window)
  * Screen lock: draw attention to what matters right now
  * Communication: send text messages to students
  * Start and end lessons: log in and log out users all at once
  * Screenshots: record learning progress and document infringements
  * Programs & websites: launch programs and open website URLs remotely
  * Teaching material: distribute and open documents, images and videos easily
  * Administration: power on/off and reboot computers remotely


## License

Copyright (c) 2004-2026 Tobias Junghans / Veyon Solutions.

See the file COPYING for the GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE.


## Installation and configuration

Please refer to the official Veyon Administrator Manual at https://docs.veyon.io/en/latest/admin/index.html
for information on the installation and configuration of Veyon.


## Usage

Please refer to the official Veyon User Manual at https://docs.veyon.io/en/latest/user/index.html
for information on how to use Veyon.


## Veyon on Linux

### Downloading sources

First grab the latest sources by cloning the Git repository and fetching all submodules:

	git clone --recursive https://github.com/veyon/veyon.git && cd veyon


### Installing dependencies

Requirements for Debian-based distributions:

- Build tools: g++ libc6-dev make cmake dpkg-dev
- Qt5: qtbase5-dev qtbase5-private-dev qtbase5-dev-tools qttools5-dev qttools5-dev-tools
- X11: xorg-dev libxtst-dev libfakekey-dev
- libjpeg: libjpeg-dev provided by libjpeg-turbo8-dev or libjpeg62-turbo-dev
- zlib: zlib1g-dev
- OpenSSL: libssl-dev
- PAM: libpam0g-dev
- procps: libprocps-dev
- LZO: liblzo2-dev
- QCA: libqca-qt5-2-dev
- LDAP: libldap2-dev
- SASL: libsasl2-dev

As root you can run

	apt install g++ libc6-dev make cmake qtbase5-dev qtbase5-private-dev \
	            qtbase5-dev-tools qttools5-dev qttools5-dev-tools \
	            xorg-dev libxtst-dev libfakekey-dev libjpeg-dev zlib1g-dev libssl-dev libpam0g-dev \
	            libprocps-dev liblzo2-dev libqca-qt5-2-dev libldap2-dev \
	            libsasl2-dev



Requirements for RedHat-based distributions:

- Build tools: gcc-c++ make cmake rpm-build
- Qt5: qt5-devel qt5-qtbase-private-devel
- X11: libXtst-devel libXrandr-devel libXinerama-devel libXcursor-devel libXrandr-devel libXdamage-devel libXcomposite-devel libXfixes-devel libfakekey-devel
- libjpeg: libjpeg-turbo-devel
- zlib: zlib-devel
- OpenSSL: openssl-devel
- PAM: pam-devel
- procps: procps-devel
- LZO: lzo-devel
- QCA: qca-devel qca-qt5-devel
- LDAP: openldap-devel
- SASL: cyrus-sasl-devel

As root you can run

	dnf install gcc-c++ make cmake rpm-build qt5-devel libXtst-devel libXrandr-devel libXinerama-devel libXcursor-devel \
             libXrandr-devel libXdamage-devel libXcomposite-devel libXfixes-devel libjpeg-turbo-devel zlib-devel \
             openssl-devel pam-devel procps-devel lzo-devel qca-devel qca-qt5-devel openldap-devel cyrus-sasl-devel


### Configuring and building sources

Run the following commands:

	mkdir build
	cd build
	cmake ..
	make -j4

NOTE: If you want to build a .deb or .rpm package for this software, instead of the provided cmake command, you should use:

	cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr ..

to install package files in /usr instead of /usr/local.

If some requirements are not fullfilled, CMake will inform you about it and
you will have to install the missing software before continuing.

You can now generate a package (.deb or .rpm depending what system you are in).

For generating a package you can run

	fakeroot make package

Then you'll get something like veyon_x.y.z_arch.deb or veyon-x.y.z.arch.rpm

Alternatively you can install the built binaries directly (not recommended for
production systems) by running the following command as root:

	make install

### Arch linux

A PKGBUILD can be found in the [AUR](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/veyon/).

### PPA

This PPA contains official Veyon packages for Ubuntu suitable for use both on desktop computers and ARM boards (e.g. Raspberry Pi). Even though only packages for LTS releases are available they should work for subsequent non-LTS releases as well.

	sudo add-apt-repository ppa:veyon/stable
	sudo apt-get update

## Join development

If you are interested in Veyon, its programming, artwork, testing or something like that, you're welcome to participate in the development of Veyon!

Before starting the implementation of a new feature, please always open an issue at https://github.com/veyon/veyon/issues to start a discussion about your intended implementation. There may be different ideas, improvements, hints or maybe an already ongoing work on this feature.

## Join translation team

Veyon and its documentation are translated at the Transifex platform. Please go to https://app.transifex.com/veyon-solutions/veyon and join the corresponding translation team. Please DO NOT submit pull requests for modified translation files since this would require manual Transifex synchronizations on our side.

## More information

* https://veyon.io/
* https://docs.veyon.io/

# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

Usually, only the latest stable release series is provided with security updates. In addition, customers with maintenance contracts are provided with updates for the respective releases in use.

| Version | Supported          |
| ------- | ------------------ |
| 4.7.x   | ✔️                 |
| < 4.7.x | ❌                 |

## Reporting a Vulnerability

If you have found a security-related bug in Veyon, please contact us via email at security@veyon.io to disclose the details about your findings. As soon as we learn about potential security vulnerabilities, we will work together to analyze and fix them as soon as possible.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -e

SRC=$1
BUILD=$2

mkdir -p $BUILD
cd $BUILD

if [ ! -z "$CI_COMMIT_TAG" ] ; then
	BUILD_TYPE="RelWithDebInfo"
	LTO="ON"
	TRANSLATIONS="ON"
else
	BUILD_TYPE="Debug"
	LTO="OFF"
	TRANSLATIONS="OFF"
fi

cmake -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=$BUILD_TYPE -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr -DWITH_LTO=$LTO -DWITH_TRANSLATIONS=$TRANSLATIONS $CMAKE_FLAGS $SRC

if [ -z "$3" ] ; then
	ninja

	fakeroot ninja package

	LIBDIR=$(grep VEYON_LIB_DIR CMakeCache.txt |cut -d "=" -f2)
	BUILD_PWD=$(pwd)

	mkdir -p $LIBDIR
	cd $LIBDIR
	find $BUILD_PWD/plugins -name "*.so" -exec ln -s '{}' ';'
	cd $BUILD_PWD

	./cli/veyon-cli help
	./cli/veyon-cli about
else
	fakeroot ninja package
fi

# Generate doc

## Dependencies

We need to clone kde-qdoc-common

```bash
cd <kde path>
git clone https://invent.kde.org/sdk/kde-qdoc-common
```

## Environment variables

set in `.bashrc`

```bash
export KDE_DOCS=<kde path>/kde-qdoc-common
```

We need to define where we generate doc:

```bash
export GENERATE_DOCDIR=<kde path>/generate-docs
```

## CMakePreset.json

For generating doc we have a target in CMakePreset.json

```bash
cmake --preset generate-doc

cmake --build --preset generate-doc
```

we can show result in `$GENERATE_DOCDIR/`

SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2004-2006 Szombathelyi György SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-2.0-or-later */ #pragma once #include #include "kldap_core_export.h" #include // clazy:excludeall=copyable-polymorphic namespace KLDAPCore { /** * This class allows encoding and decoding Qt structures using Basic * Encoding Rules. */ class KLDAP_CORE_EXPORT Ber { public: /** * Constructs a Ber object. */ Ber(); /** * Constructs a Ber object from the value. */ explicit Ber(const QByteArray &value); /** * Destroys the Ber object. */ ~Ber(); Ber(const Ber &that); Ber &operator=(const Ber &that); /** * Returns the Ber object as a flat QByteArray. */ [[nodiscard]] QByteArray flatten() const; /** * Appends the data with the specified format to the Ber object. * This function works like printf, except that it's appending the * parameters, not replacing them. The allowed format characters and * the expected parameter types are: *
    *
  • * b Boolean. An int parameter should be supplied. * A boolean element is output. *
    • *
  • * e Enumeration. An int parameter should be supplied. * An enumeration element is output. *
    • *
  • * i Integer. An int parameter should be supplied. * An integer element is output. *
    • *
  • * B Bitstring. A pointer to a QByteArray which contains the * bitstring is supplied, followed by the number of bits in the * bitstring. A bitstring element is output. *
    • *
  • * n Null. No parameter is required. A null element is output. *
    • *
  • * O,o,s Octet string. A QByteArray * is supplied. * An octet string element is output. * Due to versatility of Qt's QByteArray, these three format * strings are all accepts the same parameter, but using the 's' * format the string will be encoded only to the first zero * character (a null terminated string)! *
    • *
  • * t Tag. An int specifying the tag to give the next element * is provided. This works across calls. *
    • *
  • * v,V Several octet strings. A QList* is supplied. * Note that a construct like ’{v}’ is required to get an actual * SEQUENCE OF octet strings. Also note that the 'v' format recognizes * the QByteArray only to the first zero character, so it's not * appropriate for binary data, just only for null terminated strings! *
    • *
  • * { Begin sequence. No parameter is required. *
    • *
  • * } End sequence. No parameter is required. *
    • *
  • * [ Begin set. No parameter is required. *
    • *
  • * ] End set. No parameter is required. *
    • *
*/ int printf(QString format, ...); // Passing by-value since it's used by va_start int scanf(QString format, ...); unsigned int peekTag(int &size); unsigned int skipTag(int &size); private: class BerPrivate; std::unique_ptr const d; }; }

#pragma once

/**
 * LDAP Error codes.
 * These codes taken from openldap's ldap.h, and prefixed with KLDAP_
 * instead of LDAP_, just for applications which uses the kldap library
 * doesn't need to include openldap headers
 */

#define KLDAP_SUCCESS 0x00

#define KLDAP_RANGE(n, x, y) (((x) <= (n)) && ((n) <= (y)))

#define KLDAP_OPERATIONS_ERROR 0x01
#define KLDAP_PROTOCOL_ERROR 0x02
#define KLDAP_TIMELIMIT_EXCEEDED 0x03
#define KLDAP_SIZELIMIT_EXCEEDED 0x04
#define KLDAP_COMPARE_FALSE 0x05
#define KLDAP_COMPARE_TRUE 0x06
#define KLDAP_AUTH_METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED 0x07
#define KLDAP_STRONG_AUTH_NOT_SUPPORTED KLDAP_AUTH_METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED
#define KLDAP_STRONG_AUTH_REQUIRED 0x08
#define KLDAP_STRONGER_AUTH_REQUIRED KLDAP_STRONG_AUTH_REQUIRED
#define KLDAP_PARTIAL_RESULTS 0x09 /* LDAPv2+ (not LDAPv3) */

#define KLDAP_REFERRAL 0x0a /* LDAPv3 */
#define KLDAP_ADMINLIMIT_EXCEEDED 0x0b /* LDAPv3 */
#define KLDAP_UNAVAILABLE_CRITICAL_EXTENSION 0x0c /* LDAPv3 */
#define KLDAP_CONFIDENTIALITY_REQUIRED 0x0d /* LDAPv3 */
#define KLDAP_SASL_BIND_IN_PROGRESS 0x0e /* LDAPv3 */

#define KLDAP_ATTR_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x10, 0x15) /* 16-21 */

#define KLDAP_NO_SUCH_ATTRIBUTE 0x10
#define KLDAP_UNDEFINED_TYPE 0x11
#define KLDAP_INAPPROPRIATE_MATCHING 0x12
#define KLDAP_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION 0x13
#define KLDAP_TYPE_OR_VALUE_EXISTS 0x14
#define KLDAP_INVALID_SYNTAX 0x15

#define KLDAP_NAME_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x20, 0x24) /* 32-34,36 */

#define KLDAP_NO_SUCH_OBJECT 0x20
#define KLDAP_ALIAS_PROBLEM 0x21
#define KLDAP_INVALID_DN_SYNTAX 0x22
#define KLDAP_IS_LEAF 0x23 /* not LDAPv3 */
#define KLDAP_ALIAS_DEREF_PROBLEM 0x24

#define KLDAP_SECURITY_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x2F, 0x32) /* 47-50 */

#define KLDAP_PROXY_AUTHZ_FAILURE 0x2F /* LDAPv3 proxy authorization */
#define KLDAP_INAPPROPRIATE_AUTH 0x30
#define KLDAP_INVALID_CREDENTIALS 0x31
#define KLDAP_INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS 0x32

#define KLDAP_SERVICE_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x33, 0x36) /* 51-54 */

#define KLDAP_BUSY 0x33
#define KLDAP_UNAVAILABLE 0x34
#define KLDAP_UNWILLING_TO_PERFORM 0x35
#define KLDAP_LOOP_DETECT 0x36

#define KLDAP_UPDATE_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x40, 0x47) /* 64-69,71 */

#define KLDAP_NAMING_VIOLATION 0x40
#define KLDAP_OBJECT_CLASS_VIOLATION 0x41
#define KLDAP_NOT_ALLOWED_ON_NONLEAF 0x42
#define KLDAP_NOT_ALLOWED_ON_RDN 0x43
#define KLDAP_ALREADY_EXISTS 0x44
#define KLDAP_NO_OBJECT_CLASS_MODS 0x45
#define KLDAP_RESULTS_TOO_LARGE 0x46 /* CLDAP */
#define KLDAP_AFFECTS_MULTIPLE_DSAS 0x47

#define KLDAP_OTHER 0x50

/* LCUP operation codes (113-117) - not implemented */
#define KLDAP_CUP_RESOURCES_EXHAUSTED 0x71
#define KLDAP_CUP_SECURITY_VIOLATION 0x72
#define KLDAP_CUP_INVALID_DATA 0x73
#define KLDAP_CUP_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEME 0x74
#define KLDAP_CUP_RELOAD_REQUIRED 0x75

/* Cancel operation codes (118-121) */
#define KLDAP_CANCELLED 0x76
#define KLDAP_NO_SUCH_OPERATION 0x77
#define KLDAP_TOO_LATE 0x78

#define KLDAP_CANNOT_CANCEL 0x79

/* Assertion control (122) */
#define KLDAP_ASSERTION_FAILED 0x7A

/* Experimental result codes */
#define KLDAP_E_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x1000, 0x3FFF)

/* LDAP Sync (4096) */
#define KLDAP_SYNC_REFRESH_REQUIRED 0x1000

/* Private Use result codes */
#define KLDAP_X_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x4000, 0xFFFF)

#define KLDAP_X_SYNC_REFRESH_REQUIRED 0x4100 /* defunct */
#define KLDAP_X_ASSERTION_FAILED 0x410f /* defunct */

/* for the LDAP No-Op control */
#define KLDAP_X_NO_OPERATION 0x410e

/** API Error Codes
 *
 * Based on draft-ietf-ldap-c-api-xx
 * but with new negative code values
 */
#define KLDAP_API_ERROR(n) ((n) < 0)
#define KLDAP_API_RESULT(n) ((n) <= 0)

#define KLDAP_SERVER_DOWN (-1)
#define KLDAP_LOCAL_ERROR (-2)
#define KLDAP_ENCODING_ERROR (-3)
#define KLDAP_DECODING_ERROR (-4)
#define KLDAP_TIMEOUT (-5)
#define KLDAP_AUTH_UNKNOWN (-6)
#define KLDAP_FILTER_ERROR (-7)
#define KLDAP_USER_CANCELLED (-8)
#define KLDAP_PARAM_ERROR (-9)

/* This file is part of libkldap. SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2004-2006 Szombathelyi György SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-2.0-or-later */ #pragma once #include #include "kldap_core_export.h" #include // clazy:excludeall=copyable-polymorphic namespace KLDAPCore { /*! * \class KLDAPCore::Ber * \inmodule LdapCore * \inheaderfile KLDAPCore/Ber * * This class allows encoding and decoding Qt structures using Basic * Encoding Rules. */ class KLDAP_CORE_EXPORT Ber { public: /*! * Constructs a Ber object. */ Ber(); /*! * Constructs a Ber object from the given value. * \param value the QByteArray value to initialize from */ explicit Ber(const QByteArray &value); /*! * Destroys the Ber object. */ ~Ber(); Ber(const Ber &that); /*! * Assigns the given Ber object to this object. * \param that the Ber object to assign * \return a reference to this object */ Ber &operator=(const Ber &that); /*! * Returns the Ber object as a flat QByteArray. * \return the encoded QByteArray */ [[nodiscard]] QByteArray flatten() const; /*! * Appends the data with the specified format to the Ber object. * This function works like printf, except that it's appending the * parameters, not replacing them. The allowed format characters and * the expected parameter types are: *
    *
  • * b Boolean. An int parameter should be supplied. * A boolean element is output. *
    • *
  • * e Enumeration. An int parameter should be supplied. * An enumeration element is output. *
    • *
  • * i Integer. An int parameter should be supplied. * An integer element is output. *
    • *
  • * B Bitstring. A pointer to a QByteArray which contains the * bitstring is supplied, followed by the number of bits in the * bitstring. A bitstring element is output. *
    • *
  • * n Null. No parameter is required. A null element is output. *
    • *
  • * O,o,s Octet string. A QByteArray * is supplied. * An octet string element is output. * Due to versatility of Qt's QByteArray, these three format * strings are all accepts the same parameter, but using the 's' * format the string will be encoded only to the first zero * character (a null terminated string)! *
    • *
  • * t Tag. An int specifying the tag to give the next element * is provided. This works across calls. *
    • *
  • * v,V Several octet strings. A QList* is supplied. * Note that a construct like ’{v}’ is required to get an actual * SEQUENCE OF octet strings. Also note that the 'v' format recognizes * the QByteArray only to the first zero character, so it's not * appropriate for binary data, just only for null terminated strings! *
    • *
  • * { Begin sequence. No parameter is required. *
    • *
  • * } End sequence. No parameter is required. *
    • *
  • * [ Begin set. No parameter is required. *
    • *
  • * ] End set. No parameter is required. *
    • *
* \param format the format string * \return the number of bytes appended */ int printf(QString format, ...); // Passing by-value since it's used by va_start /*! * Scans from the Ber object according to the given format string. * \param format the format string * \return the number of bytes scanned */ int scanf(QString format, ...); /*! * Peeks at the next tag without removing it. * \param size the size of the tag (output parameter) * \return the tag value */ unsigned int peekTag(int &size); /*! * Skips the next tag. * \param size the size of the tag (output parameter) * \return the tag value */ unsigned int skipTag(int &size); private: class BerPrivate; std::unique_ptr const d; }; }

#pragma once

/**
 * LDAP Error codes.
 * These codes taken from openldap's ldap.h, and prefixed with KLDAP_
 * instead of LDAP_, just for applications which uses the kldap library
 * doesn't need to include openldap headers
 */

#define KLDAP_SUCCESS 0x00

#define KLDAP_RANGE(n, x, y) (((x) <= (n)) && ((n) <= (y)))

#define KLDAP_OPERATIONS_ERROR 0x01
#define KLDAP_PROTOCOL_ERROR 0x02
#define KLDAP_TIMELIMIT_EXCEEDED 0x03
#define KLDAP_SIZELIMIT_EXCEEDED 0x04
#define KLDAP_COMPARE_FALSE 0x05
#define KLDAP_COMPARE_TRUE 0x06
#define KLDAP_AUTH_METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED 0x07
#define KLDAP_STRONG_AUTH_NOT_SUPPORTED KLDAP_AUTH_METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED
#define KLDAP_STRONG_AUTH_REQUIRED 0x08
#define KLDAP_STRONGER_AUTH_REQUIRED KLDAP_STRONG_AUTH_REQUIRED
#define KLDAP_PARTIAL_RESULTS 0x09 /* LDAPv2+ (not LDAPv3) */

#define KLDAP_REFERRAL 0x0a /* LDAPv3 */
#define KLDAP_ADMINLIMIT_EXCEEDED 0x0b /* LDAPv3 */
#define KLDAP_UNAVAILABLE_CRITICAL_EXTENSION 0x0c /* LDAPv3 */
#define KLDAP_CONFIDENTIALITY_REQUIRED 0x0d /* LDAPv3 */
#define KLDAP_SASL_BIND_IN_PROGRESS 0x0e /* LDAPv3 */

#define KLDAP_ATTR_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x10, 0x15) /* 16-21 */

#define KLDAP_NO_SUCH_ATTRIBUTE 0x10
#define KLDAP_UNDEFINED_TYPE 0x11
#define KLDAP_INAPPROPRIATE_MATCHING 0x12
#define KLDAP_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION 0x13
#define KLDAP_TYPE_OR_VALUE_EXISTS 0x14
#define KLDAP_INVALID_SYNTAX 0x15

#define KLDAP_NAME_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x20, 0x24) /* 32-34,36 */

#define KLDAP_NO_SUCH_OBJECT 0x20
#define KLDAP_ALIAS_PROBLEM 0x21
#define KLDAP_INVALID_DN_SYNTAX 0x22
#define KLDAP_IS_LEAF 0x23 /* not LDAPv3 */
#define KLDAP_ALIAS_DEREF_PROBLEM 0x24

#define KLDAP_SECURITY_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x2F, 0x32) /* 47-50 */

#define KLDAP_PROXY_AUTHZ_FAILURE 0x2F /* LDAPv3 proxy authorization */
#define KLDAP_INAPPROPRIATE_AUTH 0x30
#define KLDAP_INVALID_CREDENTIALS 0x31
#define KLDAP_INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS 0x32

#define KLDAP_SERVICE_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x33, 0x36) /* 51-54 */

#define KLDAP_BUSY 0x33
#define KLDAP_UNAVAILABLE 0x34
#define KLDAP_UNWILLING_TO_PERFORM 0x35
#define KLDAP_LOOP_DETECT 0x36

#define KLDAP_UPDATE_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x40, 0x47) /* 64-69,71 */

#define KLDAP_NAMING_VIOLATION 0x40
#define KLDAP_OBJECT_CLASS_VIOLATION 0x41
#define KLDAP_NOT_ALLOWED_ON_NONLEAF 0x42
#define KLDAP_NOT_ALLOWED_ON_RDN 0x43
#define KLDAP_ALREADY_EXISTS 0x44
#define KLDAP_NO_OBJECT_CLASS_MODS 0x45
#define KLDAP_RESULTS_TOO_LARGE 0x46 /* CLDAP */
#define KLDAP_AFFECTS_MULTIPLE_DSAS 0x47

#define KLDAP_OTHER 0x50

/* LCUP operation codes (113-117) - not implemented */
#define KLDAP_CUP_RESOURCES_EXHAUSTED 0x71
#define KLDAP_CUP_SECURITY_VIOLATION 0x72
#define KLDAP_CUP_INVALID_DATA 0x73
#define KLDAP_CUP_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEME 0x74
#define KLDAP_CUP_RELOAD_REQUIRED 0x75

/* Cancel operation codes (118-121) */
#define KLDAP_CANCELLED 0x76
#define KLDAP_NO_SUCH_OPERATION 0x77
#define KLDAP_TOO_LATE 0x78

#define KLDAP_CANNOT_CANCEL 0x79

/* Assertion control (122) */
#define KLDAP_ASSERTION_FAILED 0x7A

/* Experimental result codes */
#define KLDAP_E_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x1000, 0x3FFF)

/* LDAP Sync (4096) */
#define KLDAP_SYNC_REFRESH_REQUIRED 0x1000

/* Private Use result codes */
#define KLDAP_X_ERROR(n) KLDAP_RANGE((n), 0x4000, 0xFFFF)

#define KLDAP_X_SYNC_REFRESH_REQUIRED 0x4100 /* defunct */
#define KLDAP_X_ASSERTION_FAILED 0x410f /* defunct */

/* for the LDAP No-Op control */
#define KLDAP_X_NO_OPERATION 0x410e

/** API Error Codes
 *
 * Based on draft-ietf-ldap-c-api-xx
 * but with new negative code values
 */
#define KLDAP_API_ERROR(n) ((n) < 0)
#define KLDAP_API_RESULT(n) ((n) <= 0)

#define KLDAP_SERVER_DOWN (-1)
#define KLDAP_LOCAL_ERROR (-2)
#define KLDAP_ENCODING_ERROR (-3)
#define KLDAP_DECODING_ERROR (-4)
#define KLDAP_TIMEOUT (-5)
#define KLDAP_AUTH_UNKNOWN (-6)
#define KLDAP_FILTER_ERROR (-7)
#define KLDAP_USER_CANCELLED (-8)
#define KLDAP_PARAM_ERROR (-9)
#define KLDAP_NO_MEMORY (-10)
#define KLDAP_CONNECT_ERROR (-11)
#define KLDAP_NOT_SUPPORTED (-12)
#define KLDAP_CONTROL_NOT_FOUND (-13)
#define KLDAP_NO_RESULTS_RETURNED (-14)
#define KLDAP_MORE_RESULTS_TO_RETURN (-15) /* Obsolete */
#define KLDAP_CLIENT_LOOP (-16)
#define KLDAP_REFERRAL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (-17)

/*
 * KLDAP Specific
 */

nodes.code:
# Pull Requests

* Make sure you only include relevant changes in your commit(s). In particular, don't re-format
  whole source files as those indentation changes add a lot of unrelated changes to your commit.

* Make your commits as [atomic as possible](https://www.freshconsulting.com/atomic-commits/).
   * Fundamental question 1: what could we need to revert later?
   * Fundamental question 2: what could we need to cherry-pick?
   * Fundamental question 3: is there an _and_ in the commit message? -> split it!

* Adhere to the commit message [guidelines](https://chris.beams.io/posts/git-commit/):
   * Start with the module you are changing, ended with a ':'. Common ones used here are "CMake:"
     or "examples:" or "libvncclient:", but there are more! A good way to find common module
     descriptions is to look into the git history of the project.
   * Keep the commit message short and in the form of "When applied, this commit will ' `<your commit message>`
   * Do _not_ end the subject line with a '.'.
   * Example: `warpdrive: increase fuel capacity to 100k`

nodes.title: HISTORY.md
nodes.code:
This is the original author Dscho's account on the project's initial history.
If you want to know what happened afterwards, have a look at [NEWS](NEWS.md).

History
=======

LibVNCServer is based on Tridia VNC and OSXvnc, which in turn are based on
the original code from ORL/AT&T.

When I began hacking with computers, my first interest was speed. So, when I
got around assembler, I programmed the floppy to do much of the work, because
its clock rate was higher than that of my C64. This was my first experience
with client/server techniques.

When I came around Xwindows (much later), I was at once intrigued by the
elegance of such connectedness between the different computers. I used it
a lot - not the least priority lay on games. However, when I tried it over
modem from home, it was no longer that much fun.

When I started working with ASP (Application Service Provider) programs, I
tumbled across Tarantella and Citrix. Being a security fanatic, the idea of
running a server on windows didn't appeal to me, so Citrix went down the
basket. However, Tarantella has its own problems (security as well as the
high price). But at the same time somebody told me about this "great little
administrator's tool" named VNC. Being used to windows programs' sizes, the
surprise was reciprocal inverse to the size of VNC!

At the same time, the program "rdesktop" (a native Linux client for the
Terminal Services of Windows servers) came to my attention. There where even
works under way to make a protocol converter "rdp2vnc" out of this. However,
my primary goal was a slow connection and rdp2vnc could only speak RRE
encoding, which is not that funny with just 5kB/s. Tim Edmonds, the original
author of rdp2vnc, suggested that I adapt it to Hextile Encoding, which is
better. I first tried that, but had no success at all (crunchy pictures).

Also, I liked the idea of an HTTP server included and possibly other
encodings like the Tight Encodings from Const Kaplinsky. So I started looking
for libraries implementing a VNC server where I could steal what I can't make.
I found some programs based on the demo server from AT&T, which was also the
basis for rdp2vnc (can only speak Raw and RRE encoding). There were some
rumors that GGI has a VNC backend, but I didn't find any code, so probably
there wasn't a working version anyway.

All of a sudden, everything changed: I read on freshmeat that "OSXvnc" was
released. I looked at the code and it was not much of a problem to work out
a simple server - using every functionality there is in Xvnc. It became clear
to me that I *had* to build a library out of it, so everybody can use it.
Every change, every new feature can propagate to every user of it.

It also makes everything easier:
 You don't care about the cursor, once set (or use the standard cursor).
You don't care about those sockets. You don't care about encodings.
You just change your frame buffer and inform the library about it. Every once
in a while you call rfbProcessEvents and that's it.

# 2024-12-22: Version 0.9.15

0.9.15 sees some internal code structure cleanup, UTF-8 clipboard handling improvements
and HTTP server support for multithreaded VNC servers. [27 issues and pull requests](https://github.com/LibVNC/libvncserver/issues?q=milestone%3A%22Release+0.9.15%22+is%3Aclosed) were closed/merged since 0.9.14.

## Overall changes:

  * Added fuzzing with OSS-Fuzz thanks to Catena Cyber.
  * Improved build system to have files where they are expected in contemporary open source projects.
    Also split out Mac OS server example to own repo at https://github.com/LibVNC/macVNC
  * Added Windows CI on GitHub.

## LibVNCServer/LibVNCClient:

  * Fixed building with OpenSSL >= 3.0.0.
  * Fixed UTF-8 clipboard handling compatibility cases.

## LibVNCClient:

  * Fixed LibVNCClient handling of UltraVNC MSLogonII when built with OpenSSL.
  * Added UTF-8 clipboard handling.
  * Added API to allow the client to specify a subregion of the server's framebuffer and
    have LibVNCClient only ask for this, not the whole framebuffer.
  * Fixed Tight decoding endianness issues.
  * Added a Qt-based client example.

## LibVNCServer:

  * Added a proof-of-concept X11 example server.
  * Improved SSH example by having it use [libsshtunnel](https://github.com/bk138/libsshtunnel/) instead of custom code.
  * Fixed HTTPD for multithreaded servers.
  * Fixed UTF-8 clipboard crash.

# 2022-12-18: Version 0.9.14

0.9.14 represents a gradual improvement over 0.9.13 with lots of developments all over
the place. [40 issues and pull requests](https://github.com/LibVNC/libvncserver/issues?q=milestone%3A%22Release+0.9.14%22+is%3Aclosed)
were closed/merged with this release. Highlights on the LibVNCServer side are a
refined multi-threaded implementation, support for Unicode clipboard data 📋❗ and an
outbound-connection machinery that works for real world use cases. LibVNCClient received
support for [SetDesktopSize](https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#setdesktopsize)
(which had been added server-side in 0.9.13) and a properly documented SSH-tunneling
setup.

## Overall changes:

  * Added more documentation (build system integration, repeater setup) and a legal FAQ.
  * Added [contribution guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md).
  * Ported the TravisCI continous integration machinery to GitHub workflows.

## LibVNCServer/LibVNCClient:

  * Added [qemu extended key event](https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#qemu-extended-key-event-message)
    support.
  * Fixed several potential multiplication overflows.

## LibVNCClient:

  * Fixes of several memory leaks and buffer overflows.
  * Added UltraVNC's MSLogonII authentication scheme.
  * Fixed TLS interoperability with GnuTLS servers.
  * Fixed detection of newer UltraVNC and TightVNC servers.
  * Added support for [SetDesktopSize](https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#setdesktopsize).
  * Added SSH tunneling example using libssh2.
  * Added some extensions to VeNCrypt in order to be compatible with a wider range of servers.

## LibVNCServer:

  * Fixes to the multi-threaded server implementation which should be a lot more sound now.
  * Fixed TightVNC-filetransfer file upload for 64-bit systems.
  * Fixes of crashes in the zlib compression.
  * Added support for [UTF8 clipboard data](https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#extended-clipboard-pseudo-encoding).
  * Fixed visual artifacts in framebuffer on ARM platforms.
  * Fixed several WebSockets bugs.
  * Fixed the UltraVNC-style repeater example. 
  * Added support for larger framebuffers (two 4k screens possible now).
  * Added support for timeouts for outbound connections (to repeaters for instance).
  * Fixed out-of-bounds memory access in Tight encoding.


# 2020-06-13: Version 0.9.13

0.9.13 truly is a cross-platform release, the best we've ever done in that respect:
Out of the [49 issues](https://github.com/LibVNC/libvncserver/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A%22Release+0.9.13%22)
closed with this release, 20 alone were related to MS Windows. The result is that 0.9.13
is the first release with full support for Microsoft Windows! The cross-platform focused
work did not end there tough: MacOS support was brought up from barebones to a fully working
production-grade VNC server application. Other highlights are improvements regarding TLS
in LibVNCClient, [SetDesktopSize](https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#setdesktopsize)
support in LibVNCServer and a major cleanup of the project's documentation. Last but not
least, 0.9.13 comes with the usual assortment of bugfixes and security improvements.

## Overall changes:
  * Small tweaks to the CMake build system.
  * The macOS server example was overhauled and is now the most feature-complete sample
	application of the project, ready for real-world use.
  * Lots of documentation updates and markdownifying.
  * The TravisCI continuous integration now also build-checks cross-compilation from
	Linux to Windows.
  * Setup a [Gitter community chat](https://gitter.im/LibVNC/libvncserver) for the project.

## LibVNCServer/LibVNCClient:
  * Both LibVNCServer and LibVNCClient now support an additional platform, namely
	Microsoft Windows. Building is supported with Visual Studio as well as MingGW.
  * The separate crypto routines used by LibVNCClient and LibVNCServer were refactored
	into an implementation common to both libraries.
  * Several security issues got fixed, namely:
     - CVE-2018-21247: When connecting to a repeater, only send initialised string
     - CVE-2019-20839: libvncclient: bail out if unix socket name would overflow
     - CVE-2019-20840: fix crash because of unaligned accesses in hybiReadAndDecode()
     - CVE-2020-14396: libvncclient/tls_openssl: do not deref a NULL pointer
     - CVE-2020-14397: libvncserver: add missing NULL pointer checks
     - CVE-2020-14398: libvncclient: handle half-open TCP connections
     - CVE-2020-14399: libvncclient: fix pointer aliasing/alignment issue
     - CVE-2020-14400: libvncserver: fix pointer aliasing/alignment issue
     - CVE-2020-14401: libvncserver: scale: cast to 64 bit before shifting
     - CVE-2020-14402: libvncserver: encodings: prevent OOB accesses
     - CVE-2020-14403: encodings: prevent OOB accesses
     - CVE-2020-14404: libvncserver: encodings: prevent OOB accesses
     - CVE-2020-14405: libvncclient/rfbproto: limit max textchat size
  * The bundled noVNC client is now at version 1.1.0 and included via a git submodule.

## LibVNCClient:
  * Added connect timeout as well as read timeout support thanks to Tobias Junghans.
  * Both TLS backends now do proper locking of network operations when multi-threaded
    thanks to Gaurav Ujjwal.
  * Fixed regression in Tight/Raw decoding introduced in 0.9.12 thanks to DRC.
  * Fixed encrypted conne

nodes.code:
[![CI](https://github.com/LibVNC/libvncserver/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/LibVNC/libvncserver/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Build status](https://ci.appveyor.com/api/projects/status/fao6m1md3q4g2bwn/branch/master?svg=true)](https://ci.appveyor.com/project/bk138/libvncserver/branch/master)
[![Help making this possible](https://img.shields.io/badge/liberapay-donate-yellow.png)](https://liberapay.com/LibVNC/donate) [![Join the chat at https://gitter.im/LibVNC/libvncserver](https://badges.gitter.im/LibVNC/libvncserver.svg)](https://gitter.im/LibVNC/libvncserver?utm_source=badge&utm_medium=badge&utm_campaign=pr-badge&utm_content=badge)

LibVNCServer: A library for easy implementation of a VNC server.
Copyright (C) 2001-2003 Johannes E. Schindelin

If you have a general question, it's best to [ask in the community chat](https://gitter.im/LibVNC/libvncserver). If your concern is about a bug or feature request instead, please use [the issue tracker](https://github.com/LibVNC/libvncserver/issues).

If you already used LibVNCServer, you probably want to read [NEWS](NEWS.md).

What is it?
===========

[VNC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_Network_Computing) is a set of programs
using the [RFB (Remote Frame Buffer)](https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst)
protocol. They are designed to "export" a frame buffer via net: you set up a server and can
connect to it via VNC viewers. If the server supports WebSockets (which LibVNCServer does), 
you can also connect using an in-browser VNC viewer like [noVNC](https://novnc.com). 

It is already in wide use for administration, but it is not that easy to program a server yourself.

This has been changed by LibVNCServer.

Projects using it
=================

The [homepage has a tentative list](https://libvnc.github.io/#projects-using) of
all the projects using either LibVNCServer or LibVNCClient or both.

RFB Protocol Support Status
===========================

## [Security Types](https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#712security)

|Name               |Number      | LibVNCServer | LibVNCClient |
|-------------------|------------|--------------|--------------|
|None               |          1 |            ✔ |            ✔ |
|VNC Authentication |          2 |            ✔ |            ✔ |
|SASL               |         20 |              |            ✔ |
|MSLogon            | 0xfffffffa |              |            ✔ |
|Apple ARD          |         30 |              |            ✔ |
|TLS                |         18 |              |            ✔ |
|VeNCrypt           |         19 |              |            ✔ |
|UltraVNC MSLogonII |        113 |              |            ✔ |

## [Encodings](https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#76encodings)

| Name     | Number | LibVNCServer | LibVNCClient |
|----------|--------|--------------|--------------|
| Raw      | 1      | ✔            | ✔            |
| CopyRect | 2      | ✔            | ✔            |
| RRE      | 3      | ✔            | ✔            |
| CoRRE    | 4      | ✔            | ✔            |
| Hextile  | 5      | ✔            | ✔            |
| Zlib     | 6      | ✔            | ✔            |
| Tight    | 7      | ✔            | ✔            |
| Ultra    | 9      | ✔            | ✔            |
| TRLE     | 15     |              | ✔            |
| ZRLE     | 16     | ✔            | ✔            |
| ZYWRLE   | 17     | ✔            | ✔            |
| TightPNG | -260   | ✔            |              |

## Transports

| Name                       | LibVNCServer | LibVNCClient |
|----------------------------|--------------|--------------|
| RFB                        | ✔            | ✔            |
| Encrypted RFB via VeNCrypt |              | ✔            |
| Encrypted RFB via AnonTLS  |              | ✔            |
| Websockets                 | ✔            |              |
| Encrypted Websockets       | ✔            |              |


How to build
============

LibVNCServer uses CMake, which you can download [here](https://cmake.org/download/)
or, better yet, install using your platform's package manager (apt, yum, brew, macports,
chocolatey, etc.).

You can then build via:

    mkdir build
    cd build
    cmake ..
    cmake --build .

Crypto support in LibVNCClient and LibVNCServer can use different backends:

 * OpenSSL   (`-DWITH_OPENSSL=ON -DWITH_GCRYPT=OFF`)
   * Supports all authentication methods in LibVNCClient and LibVNCServer.
   * Supports WebSockets in LibVNCServer.
 * Libgcrypt (`-DWITH_OPENSSL=OFF -DWITH_GCRYPT=ON`)
   * Supports all authentication methods in LibVNCClient and LibVNCServer.
   * Supports WebSockets in LibVNCServer.
 * Included  (`-DWITH_OPENSSL=OFF -DWITH_GCRYPT=OFF`)
   * Supports _only VNC authentication_ in LibVNCClient and LibVNCServer.
   * Supports WebSockets in LibVNCServer.

Transport Layer Security support in LibVNCClient and LibVNCServer can use:

 * OpenSSL (`-DWITH_OPENSSL=ON -DWITH_GNUTLS=OFF`)
 * GnuTLS  (`-DWITH_OPENSSL=OFF -DWITH_GNUTLS=ON`)

For some more comprehensive examples that include installation of dependencies, see
the [Unix CI](.travis.yml) and [Windows CI](.appveyor.yml) build setups.

Crosscompiling from Unix to Android
-----------------------------------

See https://developer.android.com/ndk/guides/cmake.html as a reference,
but basically it boils down to:

    mkdir build
    cd build
    cmake .. -DANDROID_NDK=<path> -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=<path> -DANDROID_NATIVE_API_LEVEL=<API level you want>
    cmake --build .

Crosscompiling from Linux to Windows
------------------------------------

Tested with MinGW-w64 on Debian, which you should install via `sudo apt install mingw-w64`.
You can make use of the [provided toolchainfile](cmake/Toolchain-cross-mingw32-linux.cmake).
It sets CMake to expect (optional) win32 dependencies like libjpeg and friends
in the `deps` directory. Note that you need (probably self-built) development packages for
win32, the `-dev` packages coming with your distribution won't work. Also note that you'll
need to put `libwinpthread-1.dll` in the build dir to run the examples. You can find this DLL
on your Linux build machine via `locate libwinpthread-1.dll`.


	mkdir build
	cd build
	cmake -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=../cmake/Toolchain-cross-mingw32-linux.cmake ..
	cmake --build .

Cutting a Release
-----------------

* [ ] Update AUTHORS.
* [ ] Update NEWS.
* [ ] Update git submodules.
* [ ] Increment version in CMakeLists.txt
* [ ] Update Doxygen API docs at https://libvnc.github.io/doc/html/
* [ ] Update ChangeLog (using [git2cl](utils/git2cl.pl))


How to use
==========

See the [LibVNCServer API intro documentation](https://libvnc.github.io/doc/html/libvncserver_doc.html)
for how to create a server instance, wire up input handlers and handle cursors.

In c

# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

We fix security problems on the master branch. Downstream packagers are
advised to cherry-pick those onto release versions. Currently, no point
releases of already-released versions are made due to low development
team head count.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

Please use [this form](https://github.com/LibVNC/libvncserver/security/advisories/new).
